examples.ko: 혼자 궁상을 떨지 말고 밥 먹으러 와요.
examples.en: Don't sit alone being miserable, come over and eat.

examples.ko: 혼자 사는 게 궁상이라고 생각하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't think living alone is pathetic.
It's before payday, so I'm the picture of poverty.

examples.ko: 집에서 라면만 먹는 제 모습이 궁상 같아요.
examples.en: Me eating only ramen at home looks kind of pathetic.

examples.ko: 다 큰 어른이 궁상이나 부릴 수는 없어요.
examples.en: A grown adult can't just act all shabby and miserable.

examples.ko: 그 사람의 궁상은 하루 이틀이 아니에요.
examples.en: His penny-pinching, shabby ways are nothing new.

explain: 가난하거나 초라해 보이는 모습을 말하는데, 주로 자기 모습을 낮춰 말하거나 가까운 사이에서 핀잔을 줄 때 써요. '궁상을 떨다', '궁상을 부리다'처럼 함께 쓰는 말을 기억해 두세요.

phrases.example: 돈이 있어도 궁상을 부리는 사람이 있어요.
phrases.en: Some people act poor even when they have money.
phrases.nuance_ko: '궁상을 떨다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation used much like 궁상을 떨다.

phrases.en: Eating alone feels a bit pathetic.
phrases.nuance_ko: '궁상'이 느껴지는 모습을 형용사로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adjective form for something that looks shabby.

phrases.example: 비 오는 날 집에서 라면만 먹으면 궁상이에요.
phrases.en: Eating only ramen at home on a rainy day is kind of sad.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-이다'로 어떤 모습을 가볍게 평가할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with -이다 to lightly judge a scene as pitiful.

explain_en: It describes looking poor or shabby, and is mostly used for putting yourself down or teasing someone close. Remember its common partners, such as '궁상을 떨다' and '궁상을 부리다'.

en: to be idle; to be indolent

examples.en: I spent the vacation far too idly.
My life has become lazy lately, and I'm worried.
I get up early to fix my lazy habits.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 나태해 보여도 맡은 일은 끝까지 해요.
examples.en: He may look idle, but he finishes whatever he takes on.
Once the exam was over, my mind got slack.
I write a plan every day so I won't get lazy.

explain: '게으르다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱한 글말 느낌이에요. 몸이 느리다기보다 마음가짐이 풀어지고 해이한 상태에 잘 어울려요. 반대말은 '부지런하다'예요.

phrases.en: I want to change my idle lifestyle.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나태하다'를 꾸미는 꼴로 쓴 말이고, 풀어진 생활 습관을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used for a slack daily routine.

phrases.en: After the exam ended, my mind got lazy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 원래 부지런하던 사람이 점점 풀어지는 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a gradual slide into idleness.

phrases.en: I'm worried because I've been so lazy lately.
phrases.nuance_ko: '나태하다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A simpler, everyday word compared with '나태하다'.

explain_en: It is close to '게으르다' but sounds more formal and bookish. It fits a slack, careless attitude more than simply being slow-moving. The opposite is '부지런하다'.

en: to act frivolously; to act carelessly

examples.en: Don't be careless; check your homework carefully.
He was careless and lost his keys.

examples.ko: 시험 볼 때 덤벙대서 쉬운 문제를 틀렸어요.
examples.en: I was careless during the test and got an easy question wrong.
Because I'm careless by nature, I always make mistakes.
The children came bursting into the classroom in a rush.

examples.ko: 친구가 덤벙대면 제가 옆에서 챙겨 줘요.
examples.en: When my friend is being careless, I look after things beside him.

explain: '덤벙거리다'와 거의 같은 뜻이에요. 서두르거나 침착하지 못해서 실수하는 사람에게 써요. 비슷한 말로 '덜렁대다'가 있어요.

phrases.en: Don't rush carelessly; do it slowly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '덤벙대다'와 뜻이 같아서 바꿔 쓸 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '덤벙대다'; they can be swapped.

phrases.en: I was careless and forgot the appointment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비슷한 말로, 꼼꼼하지 못한 행동에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A similar word for not being careful or thorough.

phrases.en: I tend to be a bit careless in the morning.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는 편이다'를 붙이면 부드럽게 자기 모습을 말할 수 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '-는 편이다' softens how you describe yourself.

explain_en: It means almost the same as '덤벙거리다'. It is used for someone who rushes or is not calm and makes mistakes. A similar word is '덜렁대다'.

examples.en: The team is struggling because of the boss's incompetence.
If your incompetence shows, you lose people's trust.
He admitted his own incompetence.
Citizens are angry at the government's incompetence.
Incompetence can be fixed by learning.
Incompetence and laziness are different from each other.

explain: 무능은 능력이 없다는 점을 가리키는 명사예요. 반대말은 '유능'이에요. 꽤 강한 비판이라서 사람 앞에서 직접 말하는 일은 드물고, 글이나 뉴스에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The government revealed its incompetence through that incident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력 없는 모습이 겉으로 보인다는 뜻으로 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the lack of ability becomes visible, common in the news.

phrases.en: He cried, blaming his own incompetence.
phrases.nuance_ko: 능력 없음을 원인으로 삼아 자신이나 남을 나무랄 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for blaming oneself or others for lacking ability.

phrases.example: 일을 모르는 무능한 사람이라고 하면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: You should not call someone incompetent just because he does not know the work.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무능하다'를 사람 앞에서 꾸미는 말로 써요. 강한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form of '무능하다'. It is a strong word.

explain_en: 무능 is the noun for lacking ability, and its opposite is 유능. It is a fairly harsh criticism, so people rarely say it to someone's face; it appears more in writing and the news.

en: to be perfect and faultless; to be absolutely perfect

examples.en: No one in the world is flawless.
Don't think that plan is perfect.
The quality of this product isn't flawless.

examples.ko: 완전무결한 답을 찾으려다 시간이 다 갔어요.
examples.en: I tried to find a perfect answer and ran out of time.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 늘 완전무결해 보이려고 애써요.
examples.en: He always tries hard to look flawless.

examples.ko: 우리 팀의 준비가 완전무결해서 걱정이 없어요.
examples.en: Our team's preparation is flawless, so I have no worries.

explain: '완벽하다'와 비슷하지만 더 딱딱하고, 흠이 하나도 없다는 느낌이 강해요. 일상 대화에서는 '완벽하다'를 더 자주 쓰고, '완전무결한 사람은 없어요'처럼 말하는 게 대표적인 쓰임이에요.

phrases.en: He looks like a flawless person.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸며 주는 모양으로, 흠이 하나도 없는 사람이나 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form placed before a noun, describing a person or thing with no flaws at all.

phrases.en: This plan is not perfect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 써서 아직 부족한 점이 있다고 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, often used to say something still has weak points.

phrases.en: Today's presentation is truly perfect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻은 비슷하지만 '완전무결하다'보다 덜 딱딱해서 일상 대화에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but less stiff, so it is more common in everyday talk.

explain_en: It is similar to '완벽하다' but stiffer, with a stronger sense of having no flaw at all. In daily talk '완벽하다' is the easier choice, and a typical use is '완전무결한 사람은 없어요' (nobody is flawless).

examples.ko: 그는 몸도 마음도 유약해서 작은 일에 쉽게 놀라요.
examples.en: He is weak in body and mind, so he gets startled by small things.

examples.ko: 유약한 모습만 보이지 말고 용기를 내 보세요.
examples.en: Don't just show a weak side; try to find some courage.

examples.ko: 제 동생은 어릴 때 유약했지만 지금은 아주 튼튼해요.
examples.en: My younger brother was frail as a child, but he's very sturdy now.

examples.ko: 마음이 유약하면 작은 비판에도 상처를 받아요.
examples.en: If your mind is fragile, even small criticism hurts you.
He looks fragile, but he's tough inside.

examples.ko: 그 주인공은 유약해 보이지만 끝까지 포기하지 않아요.
examples.en: The main character looks weak, but he never gives up to the end.

explain: '약하다'보다 글 느낌이 강하고, 몸보다 성격이나 의지가 약한 사람에게 자주 써요. 사람에게 직접 말하면 기분이 상할 수 있어요. 반대말은 '강인하다', '굳세다'예요.

phrases.example: 그는 성격이 유약해서 결정을 잘 못 해요.
phrases.en: He has a weak personality and can't make decisions easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 몸보다 성격이나 의지가 약하다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when saying someone is weak in character or will rather than body.

phrases.en: He looks fragile on the outside, but he's tough inside.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉으로 약하게 보인다는 느낌을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone appears weak on the surface.

phrases.example: 저는 마음이 약해서 거절을 잘 못 해요.
phrases.en: I'm soft-hearted, so I can't refuse easily.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유약하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이고, 덜 날카롭게 들려요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easier everyday phrase that sounds less harsh than '유약하다'.

explain_en: It feels more literary than '약하다' and is often used for weakness of character or will rather than of body. Saying it directly to a person can hurt their feelings. Its opposites are '강인하다' and '굳세다'.

en: to be hidden; to be secret

examples.en: He met someone at a secluded spot.

examples.ko: 이 골목은 은밀해서 아는 사람만 와요.
examples.en: This alley is hidden, so only those in the know come.
It was a surprise party we prepared in secret.
The plan was very secret.
It was a secret meeting, but the rumor spread fast.
The two exchanged glances that seemed secretive.

explain: 남이 모르게 조용히 하는 일이나 장소에 써요. '비밀스럽다'와 비슷하지만, 은밀하다는 눈에 띄지 않게 몰래 한다는 점을 강조해요. 좋은 일에도 쓰지만 남이 알면 곤란한 일을 말할 때도 많이 써요.

phrases.example: 친구가 저에게 은밀한 이야기를 해 줬어요.
phrases.en: My friend told me a secret story.
phrases.nuance_ko: 남이 모르게 조용히 나누는 이야기에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for a story shared quietly, away from others.

phrases.en: The two of them met secretly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰래, 눈에 띄지 않게'라는 뜻의 부사 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The adverb form, meaning secretly or without being noticed.

phrases.en: That plan is not a secret anymore.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 이미 다 알려졌다는 느낌을 줘요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, suggesting it is already widely known.

explain_en: It is for things done or places kept quietly out of others' sight. It is like '비밀스럽다' but puts more emphasis on doing it unnoticed. It can describe pleasant things, and it is also used for things that would be awkward if others found out.

en: to be sly; to be wicked; to be tricky

examples.en: The alley is dark, so it looks sinister.

examples.ko: 그 사람은 말이 없고 좀 음침해요.
examples.en: That person is quiet and a bit creepy.

examples.ko: 음침한 분위기의 카페라서 오래 못 있었어요.
examples.en: The café had a gloomy vibe, so I couldn't stay long.
The abandoned house felt sinister even in the daytime.

examples.ko: 음침하게 웃지 말고 그냥 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Don't smile creepily, just tell me.
The hallway with the lights off is gloomy and scary.

explain: 어둡고 으스스한 장소에도 쓰고, 말이 없고 속을 알 수 없는 사람에게도 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 부정적인 말이에요. '음흉하다'는 나쁜 속셈이 있다는 느낌이고, '음침하다'는 어둡고 기분 나쁜 분위기가 중심이에요.

phrases.example: 밤에 음침한 골목을 혼자 걷기 무서워요.
phrases.en: I'm scared to walk alone in a creepy alley at night.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어둡고 기분 나쁜 장소를 꾸밀 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most often used for a dark, unpleasant-feeling place.

phrases.example: 창문이 없는 방은 좀 음침해 보여요.
phrases.en: A room without windows looks a bit gloomy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 겉모습이 어둡고 으스스하게 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when something looks dark and eerie on the outside.

phrases.example: 말이 없고 음침한 사람이라서 다가가기 어려워요.
phrases.en: He's a quiet, shady person, so it's hard to approach him.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람에게 쓰면 속을 알 수 없고 기분 나쁘다는 부정적인 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said of a person, it is negative: unreadable and unsettling.

explain_en: It is used both for dark, creepy places and for quiet people whose thoughts are hard to read. Said about a person, it is negative. '음흉하다' suggests a hidden bad intention, while '음침하다' is mostly about a dark, unpleasant feel.

en: to be omnipotent; to be almighty

examples.en: Many people believe God is almighty.

examples.ko: 전능한 힘을 가진 영웅이 나오는 영화예요.
examples.en: It is a movie with a hero who has almighty power.
AI is not all-powerful.

examples.ko: 아이에게 부모는 전능해 보일 때가 있어요.
examples.en: To a child, parents sometimes seem all-powerful.

examples.ko: 아무리 돈이 많아도 전능할 수는 없어요.
examples.en: No matter how much money you have, you can't be all-powerful.
Many people pray to almighty God.

explain: 주로 '전능한 신'처럼 신이나 신화 속 존재에게 써요. 사람이나 기계에게 쓰면 과장하거나 비꼬는 느낌이 있어요. '만능'은 재주가 많다는 칭찬이라서 느낌이 달라요.

phrases.en: That religion believes in an almighty god.
phrases.nuance_ko: '전능하다'와 가장 자주 같이 나오는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most frequent collocation with this word.

phrases.en: Humans are not omnipotent.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람의 한계를 말할 때 부정형으로 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in the negative to talk about human limits.

phrases.en: If an omnipotent being existed, would the world be different?
phrases.nuance_ko: 신이라는 말을 쓰지 않고 이야기할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you want to avoid saying 'god' directly.

explain_en: It is mostly used for gods or mythical beings, as in 전능한 신. Used for a person or a machine, it sounds exaggerated or sarcastic. 만능 is praise for being very skilled, so the feeling is different.

examples.ko: 안개 속에서 사람 같은 형체를 봤어요.
examples.en: I saw a human-like figure in the fog.

examples.ko: 불에 타서 가구의 형체도 알아볼 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The furniture burned so badly its shape was unrecognizable.

examples.ko: 어둠 속에서 아무 형체도 보이지 않았어요.
examples.en: I could not see any shape in the dark.
The snowman melted and only a rough shape was left.
The outline of a big animal moved in the distance.
The child was startled by a blurry shape.

explain: '형체가 없다', '형체를 알아볼 수 없다', '형체가 보이다'처럼 부정이나 흐릿한 상태와 자주 써요. '모양'은 눈에 보이는 일반적인 생김새이고, 형체는 물체로서의 윤곽에 초점이 있어요. 그래서 '예쁜 형체'보다 '예쁜 모양'이 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The wind has no shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 눈에 보이는 뚜렷한 모양이 없다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means there is no visible, definite form.

phrases.example: 너무 어두워서 형체를 알아볼 수 없어요.
phrases.en: It's too dark to make out the shape.
phrases.nuance_ko: 보이지만 무엇인지 구별이 안 될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you can see something but can't tell what it is.

phrases.en: I can see the figure of a person in the distance.
phrases.nuance_ko: 흐릿하게 윤곽이 보일 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an outline is faintly visible.

explain_en: It often appears with negatives or blurry things: '형체가 없다', '형체를 알아볼 수 없다', '형체가 보이다'. '모양' is general appearance, while 형체 focuses on a thing's outline as an object. So '예쁜 모양' sounds more natural than '예쁜 형체'.

examples.ko: 얼굴이 흙빛이 되어 아무 말도 못 했어요.
examples.en: His face turned ashen and he couldn't say anything.
After the long drought, the rice paddy dried to the color of dirt.
His complexion was ashen as he came out of the hospital.

examples.ko: 비가 많이 온 뒤 강물이 흙빛을 띠었어요.
examples.en: After the heavy rain, the river took on a muddy color.

examples.ko: 흙빛 벽돌 건물이 마을 입구에 있어요.
examples.en: There is an earth-colored brick building at the village entrance.

examples.ko: 그의 표정은 흙빛이라서 아주 어두워 보였어요.
examples.en: His expression looked very dark, drained of color.

explain: 흙 같은 갈색 계열의 색을 뜻하지만, 사람의 얼굴이나 안색에 쓰면 놀람, 병, 절망 때문에 어둡고 핏기가 없는 모습을 말해요. 이 쓰임은 뉴스나 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 충격적인 소식에 그의 얼굴이 흙빛이 되었어요.
phrases.en: His face turned ashen at the shocking news.
phrases.nuance_ko: 놀람, 두려움, 병 때문에 얼굴에 핏기가 없어지고 어두워진 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a face that loses color and turns dark from shock, fear or illness.

explain_en: It names an earthy brownish color, but when used for a person's face or complexion it describes a dark, bloodless look caused by shock, illness or despair. This use appears often in news and stories.
